items.key: ai:christa pike is the first person ever to survive two lethal injections — here's how
items.text: Christa Pike is the first person ever to survive two lethal injections — here's how
items.article: Christa Pike was due to be executed on Wednesday but survived two doses of a lethal injection - a doctor reveals how she could've survived. Christa Pike’s failed death row execution in Tennessee has sparked an internet firestorm after she survived not one, but two, lethal injections. She was due to be the first woman put to death in that state in 206 years, after she tortured and killed a fellow student, Colleen Slemmer, in 1995. The 50-year-old was taken to hospital after she was heard snoring behind the closed curtain, despite the attempted execution. Her survival has been dubbed ‘singular and unparalleled’ by Robin M Maher, executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center. Nine men have also survived their execution dates in the past 80 years, the most recent being Tony Carruthers , who was sentenced to death for a 1994 triple murder. His execution failed on May 21, 2026, after there were no suitable veins left to secure a ‘back up line’ which is a lethal injection protocol. But, none of those who survived actually had a lethal dose administered, until Christa. We spoke to a doctor to try and find out why.

items.text: Income tax change is coming in Budget 2027. Here’s what it means for you
items.article: How will changes in income tax bands, USC and credits affect you? T he income tax changes in the budget are set to involve moves in tax bands, credits and the universal social charge (USC) . As such, their impact on individual taxpayers could be very different, depending on how much they earn and other factors. Here is what you need to know. The most significant change for many middle- and higher-income taxpayers will be in this area. The income tax band determines how much of your income you pay at the lower, or standard, 20 per cent income tax rate. The rest of your income is charged at the higher 40 per cent rate. At the moment the top of the standard rate tax band – or the cut-off point as it is also known – is €44,000 for single people, €48,000 for a single parent and €53,000 for a married couple with one earner. Flavio Bolsonaro and current President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva who is running for reelection in Brasilia, Brazil, Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. Eraldo Peres/AP hide caption RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil—As Brazilians prepare to vote in the first round of the presidential election Sunday, they're weighing sharp differences between the top candidates on security , foreign policy , and the environment . But they're also thinking about kitchen table issues . And if you really want to know how Brazilians feel about the economy, look no further than how often picanha, the country's prized cut of beef, is on the table. When left-wing president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was campaigning for his current role four years ago, he told voters they would be able to afford picanha again if he were elected. At the time, Brazil's economy was still recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic. Picanha, or a top sirloin cap steak, is a marker of prosperity in this beef-loving country. Lula is now running for reelection in what polls suggest is a tight race with Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro . items.text: A skydiver landed on her at Burning Man. Who will pay the medical bills?
items.article: A Burning Man attendee was hospitalized after a skydiver struck her while landing. On Sept. 5, Mary Herre was on her way to a math-themed camp at Burning Man for a slice of pie when she noticed two skydivers landing in an area with lots of foot and bike traffic. Though it was a cool sight, she remembers wondering, “Why are they so close to the city?” Within moments, the 51-year-old Colorado resident heard whistling and yelling and was suddenly struck by a third skydiver on the left side of her back — the same side as her sole kidney. “I was just screaming, ‘That’s my only kidney, that’s my only kidney,’” Herre said. “I was terrified, and then I was in excruciating pain.” Herre told SFGATE that she was hit near Rampart, Burning Man’s highly equipped hospital for the temporary desert city’s 70,000 residents, and emergency services personnel saw the impact and transported her to the emergency room. It’s not the first time she’d been treated at Burning Man for an injury, as she tore her ACL last year, she said. But this time, Herre was advised that she might need to leave Black Rock City for a more advanced monitoring of her injuries, particularly her kidney. Though the hospital offered to medevac her by helicopter, Herre opted to have her son drive her to a hospital in Sparks, Nevada.
